source_of_truth: Operator directive (2026-06-07): plan-review's lock-time coupling lint flags any AC token it cannot resolve as missing_prereq (block-severity), and the resolver only knows the existing codebase vocabulary — so a greenfield/schema/contract plan that intentionally defines new symbols self-deadlocks at lock. Add a principled per-feature escape hatch (an introduces list) the lint honors with dependency ordering. Discovered while drafting plan 2026-06-07-001 (architecture evidence contract), whose enum names cannot lock. Lives in scripts/dontpanic_orchestrate/plan_review/ (lint.py + report.py + pre_lock_gate.py).
completion_test: A feature may declare an optional per-feature introduces list of identifier strings; the plan-review coupling lint treats an introduced symbol as resolved for the introducing feature and any later feature in plan order, but NOT for earlier features; a never-introduced or misspelled token still raises missing_prereq (block); the plan-review report names introduced symbols as introduced-here; plans without introduces are byte-identical to today. No change outside plan_review; no cross-plan resolution; symbols are author-declared, never auto-derived.

user_journeys.name: contract-plan-locks
user_journeys.description: A contract/greenfield plan declares the symbols each feature defines via introduces; plan-review no longer self-blocks those symbols, and the plan can reach lock.

user_journeys.name: dependency-order-preserved
user_journeys.description: A symbol introduced by a later feature does not resolve for an earlier feature; ordering reasoning is intact.

non_goals: Cross-plan symbol resolution (introduces is scoped within one plan)
Auto-deriving introduced symbols from features.json or code (authors declare them)
Any change to the architecture evidence contract plan 2026-06-07-001
Relaxing the missing_prereq block-severity for non-introduced symbols
